summary: Read from the Node Readable buffer with byte/object-mode semantics and nullable temporary-empty result.

target.notes: Runtime must preserve internal queue boundaries, optional size behavior, objectMode single-item semantics, setEncoding output, data-event side effects when a chunk is returned, and null meaning no chunk currently available.

semantics.null: may mean temporarily empty, not necessarily EOF
semantics.object_mode: returns one object regardless of size

caveats: Do not translate null from read() directly to permanent EOF without stream state.
Buffer/string boundaries and encoding decoder state are observable.

tests.name: object mode ignores size
tests.input: const {Readable}=require('node:stream'); const r=Readable.from([{x:1},{x:2}],{objectMode:true}); r.on('readable',()=>{const v=r.read(999); if(v) console.log(v.x)});
tests.expected_behavior: each successful read yields a single object, not 999 objects
